description: Detection configuration for forensictriage. Lists and thresholds are plain data: change them without touching code. Domain and tool lists are examples to tune for your environment, not a complete catalogue.

mitre.T1052.001: Exfiltration Over Physical Medium: Exfiltration over USB
mitre.T1567.002: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
mitre.T1560.001: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility

rules.title: File matches a known-bad hash
rules.description: A file's MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 is on the known-bad list.
response: Isolate the host from the network.
Preserve the file and its hashes; submit to your malware analysis process.
Search other hosts for the same hash.

rules.title: File extension does not match its content
rules.description: The first bytes of the file identify a different format than its extension claims. Severity depends on how different (executable or archive behind a document or image extension is high).
response: Treat the file by what it is, not by its name.
Check when and by whom it was renamed (timeline, MFT, USN journal if available).
If it is an archive, list its members and review them.

rules.title: Timestamps are consistent with timestomping
rules.description: Several independent timestamp indicators agree (for example $STANDARD_INFORMATION earlier than $FILE_NAME, zero sub-second digits, embedded document dates later than the file system date).
response: Trust $FILE_NAME times and other sources (browser, prefetch, document metadata) over $STANDARD_INFORMATION for this file.
Rebuild the timeline using the $FN times.
Look for the tool that changed the time (prefetch, recent programs).

rules.title: Weak timestamp anomalies
rules.description: Files with a single weak indicator, most commonly 'modified before created', which is what an ordinary copy from another disk produces. Listed for completeness, not as evidence of tampering.
response: Do not treat these as timestomping on their own.
Review only if the files are otherwise interesting.

rules.title: Deleted files recovered by carving
rules.description: Complete files were recovered from unallocated space by signature carving.
response: Hash and review each carved file.
Compare carved files with existing files and with Recycle Bin records.
Note that carved files have no name or timestamps; those come from correlation.

rules.title: Recycle Bin record without its content
rules.description: A $I metadata record survives, but the matching $R content file is gone: the file was deleted and its content removed from the bin.
response: Search unallocated space for content of the recorded size and type.
Establish who emptied or cleaned the bin and when.

rules.title: USB mass-storage device was connected
rules.description: The registry export shows a USB storage device. Severity rises to high when it coincides with archiving, staging or deletion activity.
response: Identify the device by serial number and ask for it to be surrendered or imaged.
List files opened from its drive letter (recent documents, jump lists).
Check data loss prevention logs for the same window.

rules.title: Archive utility was executed
rules.description: Prefetch shows a compression tool running.
response: Look for archives created around the run times.
Review the archive contents if recovered.

rules.title: Secure-deletion or anti-forensic tool was executed
rules.description: Prefetch shows a tool commonly used to overwrite files or change timestamps.
response: Expect missing artefacts; rely on carving and secondary sources.
Establish whether use was authorised (IT may use these tools too).

rules.title: Visits to file-sharing or personal webmail sites
rules.description: Browser history shows visits to file-transfer, cloud-storage or webmail domains from the configured lists. A visit alone is not an upload.
response: Check proxy or firewall logs for upload volume to these domains.
Look for matching downloads or uploads in the same session.

rules.title: Searches about deleting files or changing dates
rules.description: Search terms in browser history match anti-forensic phrasing. Context matters: a curious user can search the same words.
response: Read the searches in the timeline context.
Correlate with the deletion and timestamp findings.

rules.title: Staging directory with business documents
rules.description: Several documents were gathered in a folder whose name matches a staging pattern.
response: Hash and preserve the folder's files.
Compare with the archive and the USB activity.

rules.title: External indicators found in user files
rules.description: URLs, IP addresses or email addresses outside the organisation were found in files (documentation noise such as XML schema URLs is filtered out).
response: Check each indicator against proxy, DNS and mail logs.
Block or monitor as appropriate.

rules.title: MFT entries for deleted files
rules.description: The file system metadata export lists entries that are no longer in use and whose files are absent from the evidence tree. Names and timestamps survive deletion.
response: Use the names and sizes to look for the content in unallocated space.
Check the USN journal and volume shadow copies if available.

rules.title: Evidence integrity check failed
rules.description: A hash or metadata comparison before and after analysis found a difference.
response: Stop. Do not rely on results from this run.
Restore the evidence from the verified original and re-run.
Record the incident in the chain-of-custody log.
